newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German states seek bids for 2nd Jumbo bond.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German states seek bids for 2nd Jumbo bond.

text.p: Ten German federal states will launch a joint "Jumbo" 10-year bond this week, the second pooled debt issue of its kind by states keen to obtain funds more cheaply than if they sold debt individually.

The new bond, "Laender Jumbo No. 2," will carry a coupon of six percent and have a volume of 4.5 billion marks, the finance ministry for the state of Hesse said. It matures on January 29, 2007. Bids from banks are due by 1000 GMT on Thursday.

The issue exceeds the four-billion mark volume of the first pooled Jumbo sold last August, and the states hope to sell the new bond at a higher price as a result. The first Jumbo was issued by seven of Germany's 16 states, or Laender.

The states plan regular joint issues of four to five billion marks to cut borrowing costs, attract foreign investors and prepare for greater competition among borrowers after European economic and monetary union.

Bids must be no more than 16 basis points above the yield on the benchmark six-percent federal government bond maturing on January 4, 2007, the ministry said. That bond yielded 5.75 percent in mid-afternoon trade on Wednesday.

Dealers said the issue came at an opportune time for borrowers as debt yields were at record lows, encouraged by the prospect of sluggish German economic growth and low inflation, which should keep interest rates low.

But they added that bidders were likely to be aggressive in their pricing as the German market had already seen a flood of new 10-year issues this year, including the new 15 billion mark benchmark federal bon, which will be increased by up to 10 billion marks later this month.
"I'm not saying the issue is going to be a flop, but I don't think investors are going to tear the paper out of our hands," said one dealer at a major German bank who declined to be named.
"The paper is expensive, and we've already had a lot of fresh supply recently so I'm skeptical."
The bond will be placed with investors via a consortium of market-making banks.
The consortium must consist of at least three and at most six banks experienced in placing large volume debt issues and undertaking the necessary market-smoothing activities, the ministry said.
The issuing states are North Rhine-Westphalia, Berlin, Hamburg, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Schleswig-Holstein, Brandenburg, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saarland.
North Rhine-Westphalia is liable for the largest portion of the issue with one billion marks. Four states have portions of 250 million marks and five have shares of 500 million marks.
